  scenario: primary

## What this notebook checks

Compare time-of-day exposure patterns by sex using the temporal model selected
in H02. Account for autocorrelation, meaning that neighbouring time points tend
to be similar, as well as repeated measurements from participants, site
differences, and the relevant context. Interpret fitted time-pattern
components as model terms, not as percentages of observed variation explained.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the prepared H11 dataset in `artifacts/06_model_data/H11.rds` and the
  temporal model selected in H02.
- Produces: fitted models; checks of time dependence and influential
  participants or sites; comparisons of time-of-day patterns; effect estimates
  in interpretable units with 95% confidence intervals; the exact participants,
  participant-days, 30-minute observations, and sites used by each model;
  participants, participant-days, and 30-minute observations by sex, overall
  and by site; tables; figures; and exact source data.
- Fixed rule: variation in a fitted time-pattern term is not described as
  variance explained.
- Data sensitivity: fit this identical H11 implementation to the
  manuscript-prepared dataset and compare exact samples by sex, temporal
  estimates, 95% confidence intervals, diagnostics, and conclusions.
